title: Maths Foundations
description: Rearrange an equation and know why each move is allowed. Read a straight line off a graph, and read a graph back into an equation.
audience: An adult returning to algebra who can arithmetic confidently but was never shown why the rules work.

modules.title: Rearranging
modules.summary: Why an equation can be changed at all, and which changes preserve its truth.

concepts.title: Variable
concepts.summary: A letter standing for a number that is fixed but not yet known.

concepts.title: Balance
concepts.summary: An equation stays true when the same operation is applied to both sides.

concepts.title: Inverse operation
concepts.summary: The operation that undoes another, which is how a variable is isolated.

concepts.title: Substitution
concepts.summary: Replacing a letter with a value, which is how an answer is checked.

lessons.title: What a letter stands for
lessons.outcome: Say what a variable is and is not, and check a proposed solution by substituting it back.
outline: Hook: is x a number, a mystery, or a placeholder?
Explain a variable as one fixed unknown value
Definition: variable, solution
Worked example: checking a wrong answer by substitution
Check: which value satisfies the equation
Close: substitution is the check you always have

lessons.title: Keeping the balance
lessons.outcome: Justify each step of a rearrangement by naming the operation applied to both sides.
outline: Hook: which of these two steps is illegal?
Explain the balance idea
Worked example: isolating x in two steps, naming each
Interact: order the steps of a rearrangement
Check: spot the step that breaks the balance
Close: every legal move does the same thing twice

lessons.title: Undoing in the right order
lessons.outcome: Unwind an expression by reversing the order its operations were applied in.
outline: Hook: to undo 'double it then add three', what comes off first?
Explain inverse operations and reverse order
Worked example: solving 2x + 3 = 11
Interact: order the undoing steps
Check: solve a three-step equation
Close: build up forwards, take apart backwards

modules.title: Straight lines
modules.summary: The link between an equation with two letters and a line drawn on axes.

concepts.title: Coordinates
concepts.summary: A pair of numbers naming one point on a plane.

concepts.title: Gradient
concepts.summary: How much y changes for each unit of x, which is the line's steepness.

concepts.title: Intercept
concepts.summary: Where a line crosses an axis, which fixes its position.

lessons.title: A point is a pair
lessons.outcome: Place a point from its coordinates and read coordinates back off a plotted point.
outline: Hook: which comes first, across or up?
Explain the ordered pair
Worked example: plotting three points
Interact: place a point on the axes
Check: read a point off the grid
Close: order matters, and the origin is the anchor

lessons.title: How steep is it
lessons.outcome: Calculate a gradient from two points and say what its sign means.
outline: Hook: two lines, which is steeper and how would you prove it?
Explain rise over run
Worked example: a positive and a negative gradient
Interact: place a second point that gives a required gradient
Check: read the gradient off a drawn line
Close: gradient is a rate, not a position

lessons.title: From equation to line
lessons.outcome: Draw the line of y = mx + c from its two numbers, and recover them from a drawn line.
outline: Hook: what do the two numbers in y = 2x + 1 control?
Explain m as gradient and c as intercept
Worked example: sketching from the equation
Interact: place the point where the line meets the vertical axis
Check: match a line to its equation
Close: two numbers fix a line completely
